documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-week visit; he texted Friday.

Since around mid-July he has been losing weight without trying, is tired most days and coughing more. For about the last two weeks there have been streaks of blood in the sputum, mostly in the mornings, never more than streaks. No fever he has measured, no chest pain. Not smoking.
Oncology: last CT 7/14 clean (post-treatment change, no new tumor); next surveillance CT is booked for 10/29.

BP 129/81, HR 71, SpO2 96% RA, Wt 67.5 kg (77 kg in July).
Looks thinner and tired. Right ptosis/miosis. Lungs: decreased breath sounds at both apices; prolonged expiration. Heart regular. No supraclavicular nodes. Clubbing. No edema.

A/P
1. Weight loss ~10 kg since July, fatigue, increased cough, blood-streaked sputum in a man with treated stage IIIB NSCLC and COPD - needs prompt chest imaging and pulmonary evaluation. Called pulmonology: they will see him 11/13 (originally later) and get chest CT that day. Spoke with oncology (see phone note): agree to cancel the 10/29 surveillance CT so he is not scanned twice; oncology will follow the pulmonology results.

3. HTN - continue HCTZ.
4. Flu vaccine today. RSV and updated COVID next week at nurse visit.
Return precautions: heavy bleeding, shortness of breath, fever - ED.

documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY CLINIC
Date: 11/13/2025 (moved up at the request of his PCP)

Background: stage IIIB NSCLC (right upper lobe superior sulcus) treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab, with SBRT for a right lower lobe site in 10/2024; COPD.

History: For four months he has been losing weight steadily, coughing more and feeling fatigued. Over the past month he has had occasional hemoptysis. He has a 40-pack-year history and quit smoking about a year and a half ago.

Vitals: temperature 37.2 C (99 F), BP 130/80, pulse 88, respiratory rate 20, SpO2 94% on room air, weight 67.1 kg.
Exam: Cachectic. Breath sounds decreased at both apices. Clubbing. Right ptosis and miosis.

Labs: complete blood count and basic metabolic panel normal.
Chest x-ray: cavitary lesions in both upper lobes.
High-resolution CT the same day (done in place of his October surveillance scan): several cavities in both apices; one contains an intracavitary mass suggestive of an aspergilloma.

Assessment: Bilateral apical cavitary disease with a probable aspergilloma, in a man with emphysema and prior thoracic radiation; recurrent malignancy is less likely on this pattern but remains in the differential.
Plan: Aspergillus IgG serology sent today. I will contact him with the result. Copy to oncology and primary care.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Pulmonology addendum
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
ADDENDUM to 11/13/2025 visit
Aspergillus fumigatus IgG returned at 148 mg/L (reference below 40). Together with the bilateral apical cavities and the intracavitary mass on high-resolution CT, this supports pulmonary aspergillosis with aspergilloma. Discussed with the patient by phone today.
Plan:
1. Itraconazole 200 mg (two 100 mg capsules) by mouth twice daily with food, starting tomorrow after a baseline hepatic panel; planned for at least 6 months, then reassessed.
2. Itraconazole trough level and hepatic panel 2 weeks after starting (target trough at least 1 mg/L); hepatic panel every 3 months after that.
3. Itraconazole raises fluticasone and salmeterol levels. I am keeping his fluticasone/salmeterol at the same dose for his COPD and will watch for steroid side effects at each visit; he will report swelling, palpitations or new bruising.
4. Pulmonology clinic follow-up; oncology surveillance imaging continues.
Prescription sent; copy to primary care and oncology.
Pulmonology
